themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK, up 1127% from the 8-week baseline average of 1.9 complaints per week (z-score: 6.73), suggesting a coordinated tagging campaign or gang activity in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.73 indicates statistically significant anomaly
1127% spike is the second-largest deviation in the dataset
reporting_angles: Interview residents and storefront owners about locations and extent of tagging; map hotspots
Contact NYPD and Parks Dept. to determine if this is organized gang activity or copycat vandalism; ask about enforcement response

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Drug-related complaints nearly tripled THIS WEEK to 16 reports compared to the 8-week average of 1.4 per week (1064% increase, z-score: 7.57), the highest statistical anomaly in the district and an urgent public safety signal.
evidence: 16 drug activity complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly baseline average
Z-score of 7.57 is the highest statistical anomaly in the entire dataset
reporting_angles: Investigate which neighborhoods within Morris Park/Pelham Parkway are affected; interview residents about visibility of dealing, user encampments, or overdose incidents
Request NYPD enforcement data, narcotics arrests, and any ongoing operations; ask about resource allocation and community policing response

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints reached 6 THIS WEEK, a 500% spike from the 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.0), alongside damaged curbs (5 complaints 2 weeks ago, 300% above baseline), suggesting concentrated infrastructure deterioration or vandalism.
evidence: 6 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
5 curb condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.87)
Pattern convergence suggests localized infrastructure crisis on specific streets
reporting_angles: Visually survey major thoroughfares (e.g., Pelham Parkway, Morris Park Ave.) to document damaged signs, bent posts, and deteriorated curbing; photograph before/after
Contact NYC DOT to ask if these reports correlate with vehicle impact, age of infrastructure, or deferred maintenance; request timeline for repairs

themes_detail.label: Pest Population Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints nearly tripled to 12 last week from a baseline of 4.0 per week (200% increase, z-score: 4.62), aligning with the community board's recurring requests for rat control funding and suggesting deteriorating sanitation conditions.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints last week vs. 4.0 weekly average (200% spike, z-score: 4.62)
Community board has filed repeated budget requests for animal and pest control to Health and Mental Hygiene
Spike occurs amid warm weather and potential seasonal migration, but above expected seasonal baseline
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local business owners about visible rat activity, droppings, and burrows; ask about timing (sightings during day suggest severe infestation)

Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene and NYC Parks to assess whether catch basin cleaning (another CB budget request) is being deferred, and whether this correlates with ongoing rodent activity

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints spiked to 3 last week from a baseline of 0.5 per week (500% increase, z-score: 5.0), a smaller but sharply elevated public safety concern for pedestrians, particularly families and elderly residents.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Aligns with community board interest in park safety and enforcement
Potential indicator of reduced park enforcement or increased owner non-compliance
reporting_angles: Interview residents who filed complaints about where incidents occurred and any injuries or threats; canvass parks for visible off-leash dogs
Contact NYC Parks Enforcement and NYPD to ask about staffing levels, citation rates, and any hotspots; determine if dog park access is adequate
